frequency_question: How often is a complex financial sanctions package fully investigated, legally vetted, cleared through interagency review, and officially implemented within 13 days or less from initial executive directive?
membership_rule: Includes all major designation packages of Tier-1 foreign financial institutions under OFAC secondary sanctions authorities since 2010 where the implementation timeline from formal interagency tasking to public announcement was tracked. Excludes purely symbolic or routine individual SDN additions.
provenance_note: rate of 0% from only 4 case(s); too few to establish an extreme base rate -- treat as directional
coverage_note: 4 major historical precedents identified for targeted major-bank secondary sanctions; all required months of interagency dossier building and legal review.
known_gaps: Classified emergency designations under Executive Orders are not fully public regarding their exact initiation-to-completion duration, but standard interagency review (OFAC, State L, DOJ) inherently consumes a minimum of 30-90 days.
validity_reason: Administrative procedures act and interagency clearance structures remain governed by stable statutory and bureaucratic constraints.
